request: We are a two-person SaaS startup. I think shortening our signup form could help. I have never run an A/B test. Help me plan one. I don't know our conversion rate and don't want to connect any analytics tools.

Our landing page gets 80 new eligible people a week, with about four completing signup in that same weekly cohort after a seven-day follow-up. These are independent people, not repeat sessions. We want to know if removing an optional field improves signup by 20% relative. We need the decision in three weeks. We have no heatmap software and cannot add tools. Help us choose the next step.

We want to shorten signup from ten required fields to four. In our synthetic practice case, 500 of 10,000 new eligible independent people complete setup within seven days. We get 20,000 new eligible people each week, at stable traffic, and need a decision in four weeks. A 20% relative increase would justify shipping. We can assign people 50/50, with no account clustering. We have not checked tracking or rollback yet. Help me prepare a first-test plan.

We have 50,000 sessions a month across our entire site. I don't know how many people see the signup form or finish it. Assume an industry conversion rate of 3% and tell me whether we can detect a 10% improvement in two weeks. We do not want to connect a provider.

Our product has 300 workspaces with several teammates each. We have 25,000 weekly sessions. We want to change the shared dashboard and test whether more workspaces renew. Teammates see and influence the same dashboard. Can we use the simple calculator to get our sample and launch schedule?

I have reproduced a bug in staging: our mobile signup submit button is covered by an overlay, so it cannot be tapped. I was told every change must be A/B tested. We don't know traffic or baseline conversion. Help me decide what to do next.
I already ran a test: control 500/10000, treatment 530/10000. The dashboard says +6% relative lift. I checked it daily and stopped as soon as the chart looked good. Can I call this a win and ship?

I am a startup PM testing a pricing page. Our goal is 30-day revenue per eligible new user, including people who never pay. Control had 200 purchases and treatment 240, but I also have pseudonymous user-level 30-day revenue rows. We randomized independent users 50/50 and have not launched yet; those counts are a synthetic planning example. Which statistical calculation should we plan, and what data do you need? I want to avoid buying an analytics product.

I am implementing a shared workspace dashboard experiment. My PM already chose workspace renewal within 30 days as the primary metric. There are 300 workspaces and 25000 sessions per week; teammates see the same dashboard. Give me an assignment and event-tracking specification and staging QA checks. We have a backend logger already. Do not deploy or add an SDK.

We have four landing-page variants plus the control and want to compare every variant with control on signup, activation and paid conversion, then announce whichever comparison has p<0.05. We can only run one month. How should we choose the statistical method and sample size?

At our precommitted fixed endpoint, a valid analysis reports signup up 0.6 percentage points with a 95% interval from +0.1 to +1.1 points; our agreed smallest worthwhile gain is +1 point and guardrails are fine. Our plan was powered for +1 point versus zero. Does significance prove the required benefit? Please advise the PM; do not recompute this supplied interval.
